faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for SRMIST?
faqs.answer: SRM College of Agricultural Sciences, SRM Nagar: B.Sc. (Hons.) Horticulture (Intake- 90), recorded term 2024-02-08 to 2029-02-07. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at SRMIST?
faqs.answer: The college’s self-study report describes Rural Agricultural/Horticultural Work Experience. The 2024-25 brochure identifies training with agricultural GIS software.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at SRMIST?
faqs.answer: The college’s 2023 self-study report identifies practicals, field visits, experiential learning, rural work experience and educational tours. Its 2024-25 institutional brochure also describes departmental laboratories and agricultural GIS training.

Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: When was GIET’s agriculture school established?
faqs.answer: The official school account states 2017.

faqs.question: Is agricultural admission through GIETEE?
faqs.answer: The entrance page explicitly includes B.Sc. Agriculture among GIETEE programmes; the current intake rules still need confirmation.

faqs.question: Are students assigned crop plots?
faqs.answer: The instructional-farm page says separate plots are allotted to undergraduate students for crop-production activities.

faqs.question: Is the orchard inside the main campus?
faqs.answer: The university identifies the orchard at Bandhuguda outside the campus, about one kilometre away.

faqs.question: Is a current fee confirmed?
faqs.answer: A historical official 2024-25 schedule gives B.Sc. Agriculture at INR1,60,000 per year and a combined M.Sc. Agriculture row at INR1,20,000 per year. These do not establish current 2026-27 charges or a Horticulture-specific amount.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at GIET University?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; M.Sc. Agriculture — Agronomy; M.Sc. Horticulture — Fruit Science. The [courses and fees table](/university/giet-university/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GIET University?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). A full-time agricultural science degree with crop-production plots and Student READY activities.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GIET University?
faqs.answer: Historical 2020 official notice: 10+2 PCM/PCB, 50% general and 45% SC/ST; current intake criteria require confirmation.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. Agriculture — Agronomy at GIET University?
faqs.answer: The exact intake-year subject and marks rule still needs confirmation through [the official admission route](/university/giet-university/admission-process).

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. Horticulture — Fruit Science at GIET University?
faqs.answer: The exact intake-year subject and marks rule still needs confirmation through [the official admission route](/university/giet-university/admission-process).

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GIET University?
faqs.answer: ₹1,60,000 / year · 2024-25. Historical B.Sc. Agriculture annual fee, also shown as INR80,000 per semester. Other charges separate; current applicability not established. Included charges: Published programme fee; other charges are separate unless stated.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for M.Sc. Agriculture — Agronomy at GIET University?
faqs.answer: ₹1,20,000 / year · 2024-25. Historical combined M.Sc. Agriculture row, also INR60,000 per semester. Confirm Agronomy-specific current offer. It is not assigned to the separately named Horticulture course. Included charges: Published programme fee; other charges are separate unless stated.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for M.Sc. Horticulture — Fruit Science at GIET University?
faqs.answer: A verified numerical fee is not available. A dated fee schedule for the intended admission year has not been verified.

faqs.answer: The official entrance page identifies GIETEE for B.Sc. Agriculture and displays 2026-27 material, alongside a newer 2027 banner and an old 2020 fee note. Applicants need the specific intake prospectus rather than relying on mixed-year page labels. Confirm the course: Use the official programme contact to confirm that the listed degree is taking applications for your intended intake. faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for GIET University?
faqs.answer: School of Agriculture: B. Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake- 180), recorded term 2024-02-08 to 2029-02-07. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at GIET University?
faqs.answer: A dated August 2026 university report records a farmer exposure visit to Instructional Farm-I and research demonstration plots.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at GIET University?
faqs.answer: Instructional crop farms: The farm account describes undergraduate crop-production plots and research blocks. Bandhuguda orchard: The university identifies an orchard about one kilometre from the main campus.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for GIET University?
faqs.answer: Agriculture hostel allocation: The school states that five hostels serve agriculture students: three for boys and two for girls. Its description gives three to four students per room; individual allocations require confirmation. Dining and drinking water: The school describes a central mess, monitored food provision and hostel water coolers. Hostel recreation and emergency support: The facility account lists indoor games, gymnasiums and emergency ambulance provision, alongside internet access.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for GIET University?
faqs.answer: GIET’s general scholarship page contains schemes with different programme scopes, including GIETEE/Board-of-Governance categories explicitly marked B.Tech-only. Agriculture applicants should ask which government reimbursement or institutional assistance actually applies to their course and entry year. Engineering award limits should not be transferred to agriculture.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for GIET University?
faqs.answer: GIET University publishes an Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission for NIRF 2026. Its programme-duration cohorts report the graduating group, students placed, students entering higher studies and the median salary of placed graduates. These historical institutional submissions are not a placement promise or a salary estimate for every student or individual specialisation.

sections.heading: Which admission route applies?
paragraphs: The dedicated AEEL 2026 page includes undergraduate agriculture among its entrance programmes. The programme page states that admission depends on a valid AEEL rank. Reconfirm the final counselling notice and subject eligibility for the intended intake. The dated AEEL 2026 handbook specifies the agriculture PCB requirement and online application through applyug.amrita.edu. Its tentative 9–10 May 2026 examination dates are historical, not a current application opening.

sections.heading: Programme-wise eligibility and selection
paragraphs: The following requirements belong to the named programme. A university-wide entrance or eligibility statement should not be transferred to every degree.

rows: AEEL 2026 handbook: pass 10+2 or equivalent with at least 60% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Biology, and at least 55% in each of those three subjects.
Valid rank in Amrita Entrance Examination – Life Sciences (AEEL).
Confirm the intake-year subject and academic requirements.
Official programme page: M.Sc. (Ag.) in Agronomy and minimum 7.00/10 CGPA; interview-based selection.
Programme selection by interview; published 2026 phase 2 deadline was 30 September 2026 and is past.

Agriculture — Agronomy: intake-year criteria need confirmation; Ph.D. Agronomy: Official programme page: M.Sc. (Ag.) in Agronomy and minimum 7.00/10 CGPA; interview-based selection.. faqs.question: How does admission to Amrita work?
faqs.answer: The dedicated AEEL 2026 page includes undergraduate agriculture among its entrance programmes. The programme page states that admission depends on a valid AEEL rank. Reconfirm the final counselling notice and subject eligibility for the intended intake. The dated AEEL 2026 handbook specifies the agriculture PCB requirement and online application through applyug.amrita.edu. Its tentative 9–10 May 2026 examination dates are historical, not a current application opening. Confirm the course: Use the official programme contact to confirm that the listed degree is taking applications for your intended intake. Request the intake notice: Ask for the applicable selection rules, fee breakdown and document checklist before submitting an application.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Tantia University?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). A broad agriculture degree supported by a faculty farm and laboratory teaching resources.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. Agriculture — Agronomy at Tantia University?
faqs.answer: 2 years. One of the agricultural master’s specialisations in the university catalogue.

faqs.answer: The programme table lists four years and eight semesters.

faqs.question: What practical attachment model does the school describe?
faqs.answer: It names Rural Agricultural Work Experience and Agro-Industrial Attachment.

faqs.question: What is Raffles’ agriculture academic fee for 2026-27?
faqs.answer: The signed 2026-27 sheet lists INR 65,000 per year. Registration, admission and refundable security are separate one-time charges; hostel costs are additional.

faqs.question: Are scholarships automatic?
faqs.answer: The university FAQ describes case-by-case consideration by the Gomber Education Foundation, subject to its conditions and available funds.

faqs.question: Should agriculture applicants follow the general Situation Test route?

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at Raffles University?

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Raffles University?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). The programme combines agricultural science, farm practicals and a final-year hands-on component.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Raffles University?
faqs.answer: Undated official course page: 10+2 Science/Agriculture with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics/Biology/Agriculture, at least 50% aggregate.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Raffles University?
faqs.answer: ₹65,000 / year · 2026-27. Annual academic fee. One-time registration INR 1,000, admission INR 9,000 and refundable academic security INR 5,000 separately; hostel charges excluded. Included charges: Published tuition/course fee; additional charges must be checked separately.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at Raffles University?
faqs.answer: Rural Agricultural Work Experience and Agro-Industrial Attachment are described by the school.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at Raffles University?

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for Raffles University?

Its RAWE and industry-attachment account describes work outside the classroom with farm and industry communities. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What are the undergraduate subjects required in 2026-27?
faqs.answer: The booklet requires five 10+2 subjects including English and the specified Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Mathematics or Agriculture route.

faqs.question: What is the published B.Sc. first-year academic total?
faqs.answer: The 2026-27 fee sheet gives INR 1,40,000; its INR 1,21,500 tuition component is only part of that total.

faqs.question: Does tuition stay fixed across four years?
faqs.answer: The fee sheet states a 7% annual tuition increase and separately prints later-year charges.

faqs.question: Can horticulture graduates apply for entomology?
faqs.answer: The 2026-27 booklet includes Agriculture, Horticulture and Forestry bachelor’s qualifications, with its stated marks threshold.

faqs.question: Are both master’s courses covered by the checked ICAR row?
faqs.answer: The audited Faculty of Agriculture row explicitly prints B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The master’s offerings do not expand that scope.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; M.Sc. Agriculture — Agronomy; M.Sc. Agriculture — Entomology. The [courses and fees table](/university/maharishi-markandeshwar-mullana/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: 4 years. The Faculty of Agriculture’s undergraduate course, explicitly named in the ICAR register.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. Agriculture — Agronomy at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: 2 years. Postgraduate crop-management study supported by a departmental laboratory and research farm.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. Agriculture — Entomology at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: 2 years. Specialist insect-science study listed in the 2026-27 programme booklet.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: 2026-27 booklet: 10+2 with five subjects including English and Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Mathematics or Agriculture stream; 50% aggregate, 45% SC/ST.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. Agriculture — Agronomy at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: 2026-27 booklet: B.Sc. Agriculture/equivalent with 60%; 50% SC/ST.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. Agriculture — Entomology at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: 2026-27 booklet: Agriculture/Horticulture/Forestry bachelor’s degree with 60% or equivalent; 50% SC/ST.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: ₹1,21,500 / year · 2026-27. First-year tuition component. Published total academic fee is INR 1,40,000 in year 1 and INR 6,01,453 across four years; tuition rises 7% annually; hostel/transport extra. Included charges: Published tuition/course fee; additional charges must be checked separately.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for M.Sc. Agriculture — Agronomy at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: ₹70,000 / year · 2026-27. Published annual tuition component; programme academic total INR 1,67,900, additional living costs excluded. Included charges: Published tuition/course fee; additional charges must be checked separately.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for M.Sc. Agriculture — Entomology at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: ₹70,000 / year · 2026-27. University fee table has a combined M.Sc. Agriculture row; confirm specialisation-specific offer charges. Included charges: Published tuition/course fee; additional charges must be checked separately.

faqs.answer: The 2026-27 booklet gives the academic threshold for each agriculture course. faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: Faculty of Agriculture: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake- 180), recorded term 2024-06-20 to 2029-06-19. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: The faculty self-study report identifies a museum used for agricultural identification teaching and farmer training. It also describes postgraduate agronomy and entomology laboratories, with research-farm resources for crop experiments.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: Agricultural teaching museum: The report lists farm tools, machinery models, seed and other teaching collections. Postgraduate laboratories and research farm: The faculty report identifies facilities supporting agronomy and entomology study.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for MM(DU)?
faqs.answer: The faculty self-study report identifies a museum used for agricultural identification teaching and farmer training. It also describes postgraduate agronomy and entomology laboratories, with research-farm resources for crop experiments. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for MM(DU)?

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for TNU?
faqs.answer: The course page identifies experimental fields, crop laboratories and farm machinery for teaching. The older school brochure additionally describes production demonstrations. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for TNU?
faqs.answer: The approved 2026–27 fee schedule expressly excludes B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture from the university’s general 25–100% tuition-scholarship offer. Agriculture applicants should obtain written confirmation of any separate government or programme-specific support before using a scholarship in their budget.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for TNU?
faqs.answer: The university's NIRF 2025 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission reports graduates, placements, higher-study progression and the median annual salary of placed graduates for the cohorts below. The figures apply to the reported programme-duration group, rather than an individual specialisation, and do not predict an applicant's future outcome.

faqs.question: Why are two ICAR units shown for Centurion?
faqs.answer: Agriculture and fisheries have separate source rows; they belong to one Odisha university profile.

faqs.question: Does the fisheries degree use the agriculture accreditation dates?
faqs.answer: No. The fisheries record runs from 8 February 2024 to 7 February 2029.

faqs.question: Where is the fisheries school described in the regulations?
faqs.answer: The July 2022 regulations place it at the Paralakhemundi campus in Gajapati district.

faqs.question: Is agricultural engineering in the audit?
faqs.answer: Yes. B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering is included under the agriculture school record.

faqs.question: What distinguishes agriculture practical work?
faqs.answer: The school describes READY activities involving enterprise, rural and industrial exposure.

faqs.question: How are Centurion’s agriculture and fisheries fees quoted?
faqs.answer: The central table labels its Paralakhemundi rows 2026, while an older heading says 2025–26. Programme pages confirm annual B.Sc./B.F.Sc. charges and an MBA package; obtain a cohort-specific, itemised payable statement.

faqs.question: Are verified agriculture placement figures available?
faqs.answer: The NIRF 2026 agriculture/allied submission reports UG four-year programmes (2024-2025): 170 placed from 253 graduates in minimum time, with ₹4,80,000 median annual salary among those placed; PG two-year programmes (2024-2025): 37 placed from 54 graduates in minimum time, with ₹4,30,000 median annual salary among those placed. These are historical group-level outcomes, not specialisation-level placement promises.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at CUTM?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering; M.Sc. (Agri.) Agronomy; M.Sc. (Agri.) Agricultural Extension Education; M.Sc. (Agri.) Genetics and Plant Breeding; M.Sc. (Hort.) Vegetable Science; MBA Agribusiness Management; Bachelor of Fisheries Science (B.F.Sc.). The [courses and fees table](/university/centurion-university-of-technology-and-management/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 4 years. Crop, resource and rural-learning undergraduate route.

faqs.question: How long is B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 4 years. Engineering applications in agricultural production and processing.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agri.) Agronomy at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 2 years. Specialist study in agronomy.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agri.) Agricultural Extension Education at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 2 years. Postgraduate study in agricultural extension.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agri.) Genetics and Plant Breeding at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 2 years. Crop-improvement and genetics master’s route.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Hort.) Vegetable Science at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 2 years. Specialist postgraduate study in vegetable science.

faqs.question: How long is MBA Agribusiness Management at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 2 years. Management study focused on agribusiness.

faqs.question: How long is Bachelor of Fisheries Science (B.F.Sc.) at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 4 years. Aquatic production, health, processing and resource-management degree.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at CUTM?
faqs.answer: The official programme page specifies 50% in 10+2 Science and prints the subject combination as Physics/Math, Chemistry, Biology. Confirm that wording against the intake-year bulletin.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics/Biology, at least 50%; the programme page also requires a CUEE score. Confirm applicability to the intended intake year.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agri.) Agronomy at CUTM?
faqs.answer: A four-year Agriculture bachelor’s degree or equivalent with at least 50%, from a recognised university listed under UGC/AIU. Confirm applicability to the intended intake year.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agri.) Agricultural Extension Education at CUTM?
faqs.answer: Agriculture, Horticulture or Forestry bachelor’s degree from a recognised Indian university with at least 50%. Confirm applicability to the intended intake year.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agri.) Genetics and Plant Breeding at CUTM?
faqs.answer: Agriculture bachelor’s degree with second division and at least 50%, from a recognised college or university. Confirm applicability to the intended intake year.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Hort.) Vegetable Science at CUTM?
faqs.answer: Four-year Agriculture bachelor’s degree or equivalent with at least 50%, from a recognised university listed under UGC/AIU. Confirm applicability to the intended intake year.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for MBA Agribusiness Management at CUTM?
faqs.answer: Graduation in any discipline plus an entrance examination, as stated on the undated official programme page. Confirm the accepted test and intake-specific minimum marks.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for Bachelor of Fisheries Science (B.F.Sc.) at CUTM?
faqs.answer: The programme page lists PCB, biology-containing PCMB/PCBA combinations, with at least 50% for General/OBC/UPS and 40% for SC/ST/PwD. The page has no intake-year label.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at CUTM?
faqs.answer: ₹1,50,000 / year · 2026. Separate first-year B.Sc./M.Sc. Agriculture charges total ₹30,000; confirm cohort applicability. Included charges: Paralakhemundi published programme fee.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering at CUTM?

faqs.answer: Choose the agriculture, agricultural-engineering, fisheries or agribusiness route before checking entry rules. The fee table labels its Paralakhemundi rows 2026 but retains a 2025–26 heading; obtain a cohort-specific statement including other fees and accommodation. Choose the school and course: Confirm agriculture, engineering, agribusiness or fisheries and its teaching campus before applying. Check the current entry rules: Use the linked admissions portal to obtain the relevant intake-year eligibility and fee notice.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for CUTM?
faqs.answer: M.S. Swaminathan School of Agriculture: • B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (intake 240) • B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering (intake 30); • MSc. (Agri) Agronomy (inatke20) • M.Sc. (Agri) Agricultural Extension Education (intake 10) • M.Sc. (Agri.) Genetics and Plant Breeding (intake 10) • M.Sc. (Hort.) Vegetable Science (intake 10) • MBA Agribusiness Management (intake 10), recorded term 2024-03-29 to 2029-03-28. School of Fisheries: B. F. Sc. (Intake- 40), recorded term 2024-02-08 to 2029-02-07. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at CUTM?
faqs.answer: Agriculture READY activities include experiential learning, rural work and agro-industrial attachment. Fisheries regulations describe hands-on aquaponics and ornamental fish culture.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at CUTM?
faqs.answer: Agricultural research farms: The agriculture school identifies farm-based teaching and enterprise learning. Aquaculture Research Farm: The 2022 fisheries regulations describe fish ponds and a carp hatchery.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for CUTM?
faqs.answer: Agriculture uses research farms and laboratories, while fisheries has its own aquaculture teaching resources documented in the 2022 regulations. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for CUTM?
faqs.answer: The published Amrit Kaal table includes Agricultural Engineering within its non-CSE B.Tech group at Paralakhemundi/Bhubaneswar. It sets first-year fee concessions by qualifying results. This is not evidence of the same award for B.Sc. Agriculture, M.Sc. Agriculture or Fisheries, and the page does not give a governing academic year. Amrit Kaal scholarship: non-CSE B.Tech including Agri: The official table lists 10% for 60–70% qualifying marks and 15% for 70–80%; a separate top-score/JEE/OJEE band lists 20%. These are first-year fee concessions. Boundary wording, programme/campus eligibility and the current policy must be confirmed in the award letter.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for CUTM?
faqs.answer: The university's NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission reports graduates, placements, higher-study progression and the median annual salary of placed graduates for the cohorts below. The figures apply to the reported programme-duration group, rather than an individual specialisation, and do not predict an applicant's future outcome.

sections.heading: Minimum eligibility and closing rank answer different questions
paragraphs: A qualifying subject or minimum academic threshold determines whether an applicant can be considered under the applicable rules. A closing rank or score describes a particular selection list, counselling round or category. One should not be substituted for the other.

columns: If a number is described as…

paragraphs: Use the 2026 CUET mapping for bachelor’s subject requirements and the dated School of Agriculture article for master’s entry combinations. Confirm the governing prospectus, counselling route and fee statement with LPU. The live B.Sc. Agriculture page now advertises Admission 2027. The 2026 CUET mapping and dated 2026 school guidance below retain their historical session; obtain the 2027 rules before a next-cycle application.

Follow [the admission process for Lovely Professional University](/university/lovely-professional-university/admission-process) and the official notice. Seat availability and document verification remain separate from meeting a qualifying threshold.

sections.heading: Use the evidence in a shortlist

faqs.answer: 2026: 60% in a four-year B.Sc. Agriculture/Honours.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agriculture) Genetics and Plant Breeding at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2026: 60% in four-year Agriculture/Honours or Agriculture Biotechnology.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Hort.) Fruit Science at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2026: 60% in four-year Agriculture/Honours or Horticulture.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agriculture) Plant Pathology at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2026: 60% in a four-year B.Sc. Agriculture/Honours.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agriculture) Entomology at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2026: 60% in Agriculture/Honours (four years) or Horticulture.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agriculture) Vegetable Science at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2026: 60% in four-year Agriculture/Honours or Horticulture.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agriculture) Soil Science at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2026: 60% in four-year Agriculture/Honours or equivalent.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for M.Sc. (Agriculture) Floriculture and Landscaping at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2026: 60% in four-year Agriculture/Honours or Horticulture.

faqs.answer: The accredited unit is the School of Agriculture, Phagwara.

faqs.question: Does this record include agriculture master’s courses?
faqs.answer: Yes. It includes eight named master’s specialisations as well as the bachelor’s degree.

faqs.question: What is the ICAR term for LPU’s listed programmes?
faqs.answer: The audited term is 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2028.

faqs.question: What is the verified 2026 B.Sc. Agriculture eligibility at LPU?
faqs.answer: The NTA CUET UG 2026 mapping requires 60% in 10+2 with English and three subjects from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture. Confirm the age cutoff, because its age sentence still refers to December 2025.

faqs.question: Does the school show protected cultivation facilities?
faqs.answer: Yes. The official school page lists a Hi-Tech Polyhouse.

faqs.question: Can a scholarship amount be assumed from LPUNEST participation?
faqs.answer: No. LPU’s scholarship page describes several categories; the award depends on the applicable programme rules and performance.

faqs.question: Are verified agriculture placement figures available?
faqs.answer: The NIRF 2026 agriculture/allied submission reports UG four-year programmes (2024-2025): 359 placed from 449 graduates in minimum time, with ₹6,60,000 median annual salary among those placed; PG two-year programmes (2024-2025): 160 placed from 193 graduates in minimum time, with ₹7,20,000 median annual salary among those placed. These are historical group-level outcomes, not specialisation-level placement promises.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at LPU?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Agronomy; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Genetics and Plant Breeding; M.Sc. (Hort.) Fruit Science; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Plant Pathology; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Entomology; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Vegetable Science; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Soil Science; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Floriculture and Landscaping. The [courses and fees table](/university/lovely-professional-university/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at LPU?
faqs.answer: 4 years. The 2025 prospectus describes a four-year semester programme.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agriculture) Agronomy at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2 years (4 semesters). Master’s specialisation in agronomy.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agriculture) Genetics and Plant Breeding at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2 years (4 semesters). Postgraduate focus on genetics and crop breeding.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Hort.) Fruit Science at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2 years (4 semesters). A horticulture master’s route in fruit science.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agriculture) Plant Pathology at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2 years (4 semesters). Specialist postgraduate study of plant pathology.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agriculture) Entomology at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2 years (4 semesters). Master’s study in agricultural entomology.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agriculture) Vegetable Science at LPU?
faqs.answer: 2 years (4 semesters). Postgraduate specialisation in vegetable science.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Agriculture) Soil Science at LPU?

faqs.question: Where is KARE’s agriculture school?
faqs.answer: Its 2022 curriculum gives Krishnankoil in Virudhunagar district as the address.

faqs.question: Which course does this ICAR record cover?
faqs.answer: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture under Kalasalingam School of Agriculture and Horticulture.

faqs.question: What is the accreditation term?
faqs.answer: The audited term runs from 26 September 2024 to 25 September 2029.

faqs.question: What year does the quoted fee belong to?
faqs.answer: The ₹1,20,000 annual programme amount is from the official 2025-2026 table, with additional charges listed separately.

faqs.question: Is horticulture automatically covered by this agriculture record?
faqs.answer: No. The audited row here names the agriculture degree only.

faqs.question: What practical farm equipment is documented?
faqs.answer: The course page lists implements including a tractor and rotary tiller at the farm.

faqs.question: Are verified agriculture placement figures available?
faqs.answer: The NIRF 2026 agriculture/allied submission reports UG four-year programmes (2024-2025): 66 placed from 119 graduates in minimum time, with ₹3,50,000 median annual salary among those placed. These are historical group-level outcomes, not specialisation-level placement promises.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at KARE?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The [courses and fees table](/university/kalasalingam-academy-of-research-and-education/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at KARE?
faqs.answer: 8 semesters (2022 curriculum). The 2022 curriculum covers crop science, agricultural resources and extension.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at KARE?
faqs.answer: Official admissions page: 10+2 science with relevant subjects; course page additionally states 50% and specified combinations. Obtain the intake-year rule.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at KARE?
faqs.answer: ₹1,20,000 / year · 2025-2026. Historical official table also lists one-time admission fee ₹10,000, other fee ₹12,000 and application cost ₹600. Not verified as 2026-2027 fees. Included charges: Annual programme fee for resident Indian B.Sc. Agriculture applicants.

faqs.question: How does admission to KARE work?
faqs.answer: The university publishes agriculture-specific eligibility and selection information within its admissions page. The course and central pages differ in detail, so request the applying-year subject and marks requirements. Check the agriculture eligibility row: Match the 10+2 subjects with the published agriculture requirements. Confirm the selection notice: Ask for the current KCEE, counselling and fee instructions before committing funds.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for KARE?
faqs.answer: Kalasalingam School of Agriculture and Horticulture: • B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (intake 60), recorded term 2024-09-26 to 2029-09-25. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at KARE?
faqs.answer: The published curriculum includes agricultural field and laboratory subjects.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at KARE?
faqs.answer: Kalasalingam Anandammal Farm: The course page identifies a fertigation unit at the teaching farm. Farm implements: Listed equipment includes a tractor, cultivator, disc plough and rotary tiller. Agriculture laboratories: The page identifies soil, seed, crop physiology, plant protection and genetics laboratories.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for KARE?
faqs.answer: The course page documents field equipment and laboratories used for agricultural teaching. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for KARE?
faqs.answer: KARE’s admissions page includes scholarship material, but its scheme tables cover multiple programme groups. A current award and renewal rule specifically applicable to B.Sc. Agriculture was not verified.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for KARE?
faqs.answer: The university's NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission reports graduates, placements, higher-study progression and the median annual salary of placed graduates for the cohorts below. The figures apply to the reported programme-duration group, rather than an individual specialisation, and do not predict an applicant's future outcome.

faqs.question: What is IIAST at Integral University?
faqs.answer: It is the Integral Institute of Agricultural Science and Technology, which organises the university’s agriculture teaching.

faqs.question: Which degree is covered by this ICAR entry?
faqs.answer: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture, for 26 September 2024 to 25 September 2029.

faqs.question: How long does Integral list the bachelor’s degree?
faqs.answer: The institute programme page lists four years.

faqs.question: What makes the farm setting distinctive?
faqs.answer: Separate units document activities including mushrooms, weather observation, organic production and integrated farming.

faqs.question: Is IUET relevant to agriculture applicants?
faqs.answer: The university’s 2026 admission criteria identify IUET for its programmes apart from specified professional exceptions. Confirm the B.Sc. instructions before applying.

faqs.question: Are agriculture placement figures verified?
faqs.answer: No. A dated training event was found, but a cohort-based agriculture outcome report was not.

faqs.question: What agriculture fee amount has Integral published?
faqs.answer: The official Indian-applicant table lists ₹70,000 per year for B.Sc. Agriculture. Its academic year is unstated, so this is not verified as a current 2026–27 or 2027 quote; obtain a dated itemised statement.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at Integral University?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The [courses and fees table](/university/integral-university/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Integral University?
faqs.answer: 4 years. A four-year degree supported by a network of agricultural teaching units.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Integral University?
faqs.answer: The official institute programme page states 10+2 with 50% in PCM, PCB, PCMB or Agriculture.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Integral University?
faqs.answer: ₹70,000 / year · source undated; current intake not confirmed. Undated official amount; intake-year applicability is not established. This is not verified as a current 2026–27 or 2027 payable quote. Request compulsory charges, hostel and other costs separately. Included charges: Published annual programme fee in the Indian-applicant table; itemised inclusions are not specified.

faqs.question: How does admission to Integral University work?
faqs.answer: Integral’s admissions criteria page identifies IUET for its programmes other than listed professional exceptions. Agriculture applicants should use the B.Sc. eligibility entry and the current IUET instructions together. Confirm the agriculture entry criteria: Check the B.Sc. programme page against the current entrance notice. Prepare for document verification: The admissions page asks for original qualifying marksheets and certificates at interview/reporting.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for Integral University?
faqs.answer: Integral Institute of Agricultural Science and Technology: • B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake- 120), recorded term 2024-09-26 to 2029-09-25. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at Integral University?
faqs.answer: The farm page identifies undergraduate practical crop production and experiential learning.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at Integral University?
faqs.answer: Mushroom unit: Unit 5 describes button and oyster mushroom work. Weather and compost demonstrations: Unit 6 identifies an automatic weather station, vermicomposting, NADEP and Azolla. Integral Krishi Vikas Kendra: A mango-orchard setting includes an integrated farming demonstration.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for Integral University?
faqs.answer: IIAST’s farm page distinguishes practical crop production, experiential learning and processing activity across separate units. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for Integral University?
faqs.answer: An agriculture-specific scholarship schedule for Integral University was not verified. Award availability, eligibility and renewal conditions need confirmation.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for Integral University?
faqs.answer: IIAST’s homepage records a placement-oriented training and skill-development guest lecture held on 24 April 2025. This verifies a support activity, not a graduate placement percentage.

faqs.question: How can I contact Integral University about an application?
faqs.answer: Published phone: +91 9335177775. Published email: info@iul.ac.in. Official admissions: https://www.iul.ac.in/admissioninfo/Admission_Criteria.aspx

faqs.question: Which dated admission notices are recorded for Integral University?
faqs.answer: No dated admission event is verified in this profile. The official channel is https://www.iul.ac.in/admissioninfo/Admission_Criteria.aspx; check the notice for the programme and entry year you intend to join.

faqs.answer: 4 years; study format: Full time. An agriculture degree with published field and laboratory learning elements.

faqs.answer: The official 2026 landing page states 10+2 with 50% in Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Mathematics/Agriculture, or a two-year agriculture diploma with 50%.

Agriculture, Mathura campus.

faqs.question: How does admission to Shri Shivaji Agriculture College work?
faqs.answer: The 2026–27 state prospectus identifies Shri Shivaji as an aided PDKV-affiliated agriculture college, institution code 11107, with an intake of 120. Admission follows the state agriculture CAP framework. Its published final admission cutoff was 17 September 2026; this historical calendar does not establish an open vacancy. Check the official state framework: Use the 2026–27 agriculture prospectus and college code 11107 to verify candidature, entrance and reservation rules. Use the relevant CAP round: Follow registration, preference submission, allotment and reporting instructions. The published 2026–27 admission cutoff was 17 September 2026, so ask the authority about any separate later notice. Verify reporting and cost: Confirm the full document list and approved aided-college fee statement before reporting or paying.

faqs.answer: The official course page includes qualifying two- or three-year agriculture/allied diploma routes after Class 10, subject to its 50% requirement.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GKU?
faqs.answer: 4 years. A broad agriculture degree with published crop, resource and agribusiness subject areas.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GKU?
faqs.answer: Official page states 50% in 10+2 PCB/PCBM/PCM/Agriculture, or 50% in a two- or three-year agriculture/allied diploma after Class 10.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AUS?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). The 2026–27 prospectus lists an eight-semester agriculture honours degree, with separate first-year and second-year entry qualifications.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for AUS?
faqs.answer: The 2026–27 agriculture table describes government fee-reimbursement assistance for eligible APST students, subject to scheme terms and approval. The university also limits concurrent scholarship applications to one award. Its separate scholarship form deadline of 30 October 2026 is already past. Conditional APST fee-reimbursement assistance: The 2026–27 agriculture table states reimbursement up to ₹50,000 for APST candidates with annual family income below ₹2,50,000, under Central/State government schemes and prescribed terms. This is a maximum conditional benefit, not an automatic deduction or a guaranteed award; the brochure does not give renewal rules. Government stipend / scholarship application route: The university directs eligible students to Arunachal Pradesh or Government of India granting agencies and limits concurrent applications to one award. The listed university submission deadline was30October2026; no current agriculture-specific entitlement is established.

sections.heading: Minimum eligibility and closing rank answer different questions
paragraphs: A qualifying subject or minimum academic threshold determines whether an applicant can be considered under the applicable rules. A closing rank or score describes a particular selection list, counselling round or category. One should not be substituted for the other.

columns: If a number is described as…

sections.heading: Which rules should you read for your programme?
paragraphs: The official 2026–27 prospectus establishes agriculture duration, entry qualifications and an annual fee. It does not settle minimum marks or selection-test rules in the agriculture row. The homepage identifies an application portal, which returned 403 when independently opened; confirm the operative selection notice before paying.

Follow [the admission process for Arunachal University of Studies](/university/arunachal-university-of-studies/admission-process) and the official notice. Seat availability and document verification remain separate from meeting a qualifying threshold.

sections.heading: Use the evidence in a shortlist

faqs.question: Where is AUS located?
faqs.answer: The Namsai district directory gives NH-52, Namsai, Arunachal Pradesh 792103.

faqs.question: Is AUS privately funded?
faqs.answer: WHED identifies its funding as private, and the district directory labels it a private university.

faqs.question: Which agriculture course appears in the 2025 entrance mapping?
faqs.answer: Bachelor of Science (Honours–Agriculture).

faqs.question: What practical exposure has been independently documented?
faqs.answer: ICAR reported an August 2025 visit by fourth-year agriculture students to KVK Namsai at Momong.

faqs.question: What is the ICAR term for the bachelor’s programme?
faqs.answer: The audited record runs from 30 September 2025 to 29 September 2030.

faqs.question: Can the 2025 CUET rules be used for a 2026 application?
faqs.answer: They are historical evidence only. Applicants need the current university notice to establish the applicable route and subjects.

faqs.question: How long is the AUS agriculture degree, and what is its published fee?
faqs.answer: The 2026–27 prospectus lists four years/eight semesters and ₹90,000 annually. The row does not itemise every compulsory or residential charge.

faqs.question: What qualifications does the current AUS prospectus list?
faqs.answer: The 2026–27 agriculture table accepts 10+2 Science/Agriculture or equivalent for first-year entry, and an Agriculture diploma or equivalent for second-year entry. Minimum marks and selection-test rules require a separate notice.

faqs.question: Does AUS publish financial assistance for agriculture?
faqs.answer: Its 2026–27 agriculture table describes reimbursement up to ₹50,000 for eligible APST applicants with family income below ₹2,50,000 annually, subject to government scheme terms and approval. It is not an automatic scholarship.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at AUS?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The [courses and fees table](/university/arunachal-university-of-studies/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AUS?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). The 2026–27 prospectus lists an eight-semester agriculture honours degree, with separate first-year and second-year entry qualifications.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AUS?
faqs.answer: 2026–27 prospectus: first-year entry requires 10+2 in Science/Agriculture or equivalent; second-year entry requires a Diploma in Agriculture or equivalent. The agriculture row does not specify minimum marks or the selection test.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AUS?
faqs.answer: ₹90,000 / year · 2026-2027. Published annual amount for the agriculture bachelor’s degree. Obtain a complete payable statement; adjacent Life Sciences examination/OJT charges do not establish agriculture charges. Included charges: Annual programme fee in the 2026–27 agriculture table; itemised compulsory, residential and other charges are not specified in this row.

faqs.question: How does admission to AUS work?
faqs.answer: The official 2026–27 prospectus establishes agriculture duration, entry qualifications and an annual fee. It does not settle minimum marks or selection-test rules in the agriculture row. The homepage identifies an application portal, which returned 403 when independently opened; confirm the operative selection notice before paying. Select the correct entry year: Use the 2026–27 prospectus to distinguish first-year entry from diploma-based second-year entry. Confirm selection and complete charges: Request the current entrance/merit instructions and an itemised fee statement from the published university contacts.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for AUS?
faqs.answer: Arunachal University of Studies: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake- 120), recorded term 2025-09-30 to 2030-09-29. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at AUS?
faqs.answer: Fourth-year AUS agriculture students visited KVK demonstrations of climate-resilient technologies in August 2025.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at AUS?
faqs.answer: ICAR’s 21 August 2025 report describes an agriculture student visit to KVK Namsai at Momong. It supports external practical exposure rather than a claim about ownership of the KVK facilities.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for AUS?
faqs.answer: ICAR’s 21 August 2025 report describes an agriculture student visit to KVK Namsai at Momong. It supports external practical exposure rather than a claim about ownership of the KVK facilities. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for AUS?
faqs.answer: The 2026–27 agriculture table describes government fee-reimbursement assistance for eligible APST students, subject to scheme terms and approval. The university also limits concurrent scholarship applications to one award. Its separate scholarship form deadline of 30 October 2026 is already past. Conditional APST fee-reimbursement assistance: The 2026–27 agriculture table states reimbursement up to ₹50,000 for APST candidates with annual family income below ₹2,50,000, under Central/State government schemes and prescribed terms. This is a maximum conditional benefit, not an automatic deduction or a guaranteed award; the brochure does not give renewal rules. Government stipend / scholarship application route: The university directs eligible students to Arunachal Pradesh or Government of India granting agencies and limits concurrent applications to one award. The listed university submission deadline was30October2026; no current agriculture-specific entitlement is established.

faqs.answer: A dated agriculture placement report and current institutional career-support details were not verified from accessible official material.

faqs.question: How long is SRU’s agriculture bachelor’s degree?
faqs.answer: The official course page states four years and eight semesters.

faqs.question: Does the programme include rural learning?
faqs.answer: Yes. The course page includes rural work experience and other Student READY elements.

faqs.question: What school subjects are stated for direct entry?
faqs.answer: The programme directory specifies PCB with at least 55% at 10+2.

faqs.question: Is there a diploma route?
faqs.answer: The directory lists a first-class two-year Agriculture or Seed Technology diploma after Class 10.

faqs.question: What is the tuition table’s limitation?
faqs.answer: It displays ₹97,500 per semester but does not explicitly identify the academic year of that table. Obtain a dated confirmation.

faqs.question: Which ICAR term applies to the listed bachelor’s programme?
faqs.answer: The audited record runs from 16 March 2026 to 15 March 2031.

faqs.question: What tuition does SR University publish for agriculture?
faqs.answer: The undated official table lists ₹97,500 per semester for B.Sc. Agriculture, plus separate ₹5,000 enrolment and ₹25,000 one-time admission charges. The governing intake year is unverified; scholarship net fees must not be inferred from inconsistent rounded figures.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at SRU?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The [courses and fees table](/university/sr-university/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at SRU?
faqs.answer: 4 years. A bachelor’s degree with rural, experiential and industrial learning components.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at SRU?
faqs.answer: Official programme directory: at least 55% in 10+2 with PCB; first-class two-year Agriculture/Seed Technology diploma after Class 10 is also listed.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at SRU?
faqs.answer: ₹97,500 / semester · source undated; current intake not confirmed. Undated official amount; intake-year applicability is not established. Separate table charges: enrolment ₹5,000 and one-time admission ₹25,000. Do not treat this as a current2026–27/2027 payable quote or an all-inclusive attendance cost. Included charges: Tuition only in the published B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture table.

faqs.question: How does admission to SRU work?
faqs.answer: SRU’s programme directory specifies B.Sc. Agriculture entry qualifications. Confirm selection requirements and the academic year of the fee table through the agriculture admissions route. Check the bachelor’s eligibility: Use the B.Sc. Agriculture entry rather than a general engineering or science rule. Confirm fees and scholarship together: Ask for a dated payable statement identifying tuition, enrolment, admission and any concession.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for SRU?
faqs.answer: SR University: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake- 120), recorded term 2026-03-16 to 2031-03-15. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at SRU?
faqs.answer: The course page lists RAWE, experiential learning, internships and agro-industrial attachment.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at SRU?
faqs.answer: Instructional farm and horticulture garden: The course page identifies these as settings for field learning. Agriculture laboratories: The university describes laboratories supporting experiential study.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for SRU?
faqs.answer: The course page identifies instructional farm and horticulture resources, and explicitly describes Student READY learning components. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for SRU?
faqs.answer: SRU publishes an agriculture-specific tuition scholarship table with board and entrance-score categories. Its applicability and academic-year coverage need written confirmation; the separate April 2026 early-admission promotion has already passed. B.Sc. Agriculture merit scholarship table: The official page displays different tuition concessions according to qualifying scores and examinations. The draft does not assign an award to any applicant.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for SRU?
faqs.answer: SRU’s agriculture admissions material describes industry connections, skills and career guidance. A dated bachelor’s placement cohort, salary or recruiter report was not verified.

faqs.question: How can I contact SRU about an application?
faqs.answer: Published phone: +91 8331004040. Published email: info@sru.edu.in. Official admissions: https://sru.edu.in/admissions-2026/agriculture

faqs.question: Which dated admission notices are recorded for SRU?
faqs.answer: No dated admission event is verified in this profile. The official channel is https://sru.edu.in/admissions-2026/agriculture; check the notice for the programme and entry year you intend to join.

faqs.question: Where is RNBGU located?
faqs.answer: The university gives RNB Global City, Ganganagar Road, Bikaner, Rajasthan 334601.

faqs.question: How long is the agriculture honours programme?
faqs.answer: The course page lists four years.

faqs.question: Why does domicile matter when checking fees?
faqs.answer: The university publishes separate agriculture course pages for Rajasthan-domicile and outside-Rajasthan applicants.

faqs.question: What does the 2026 outside-Rajasthan agriculture fee include?
faqs.answer: The official schedule totals ₹55,000 per semester: ₹45,000 tuition and ₹10,000 examination fee. Non-refundable enrolment is ₹10,000 once; accommodation is separate.

faqs.question: Do scholarships reduce every charge?
faqs.answer: No. The 2026 policy restricts scholarship coverage to tuition and excludes charges such as examination, enrolment and accommodation.

faqs.question: Which ICAR term covers the listed degree?
faqs.answer: The audited B.Sc. Agriculture record runs from 16 May 2025 to 15 May 2030.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at RNBGU?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The [courses and fees table](/university/rnb-global-university/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at RNBGU?
faqs.answer: 4 years. An honours agriculture degree with rural work, industry exposure and production projects.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at RNBGU?
faqs.answer: Programme page states 10+2 PCM/PCB/Agriculture from a recognised board; obtain the intake-year marks requirement.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at RNBGU?
faqs.answer: ₹55,000 / semester · 2026. The official 2026 schedule lists outside-Rajasthan tuition ₹45,000 plus examination ₹10,000 per semester; Rajasthan domicile tuition ₹35,000 plus examination ₹10,000, total ₹45,000. Non-refundable enrolment ₹10,000 is one time. Accommodation is separate. Included charges: Outside-Rajasthan programme page: ₹45,000 tuition and ₹10,000 examination fee.

faqs.question: How does admission to RNBGU work?
faqs.answer: RNBGU’s procedure describes application, documents, aptitude testing, committee review and an offer specifying payment and reporting requirements. Apply using the appropriate programme category: Select agriculture and establish whether the Rajasthan-domicile category applies. Check the admission offer: The university says the offer specifies fees and the academic-session requirements.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for RNBGU?
faqs.answer: RNB Global University, Bikaner: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake- 60), recorded term 2025-05-16 to 2030-05-15. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at RNBGU?
faqs.answer: The school describes a three-week agro-industrial attachment. Live projects include nursery raising, organic farming, vegetable production and orchard management.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at RNBGU?
faqs.answer: Attached agriculture farm: The school states that an agriculture farm is attached to the campus. Agriculture laboratories: Laboratory teaching is identified in the school pedagogy.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for RNBGU?
faqs.answer: The school identifies an attached agriculture farm, laboratories and crop-based demonstrations. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for RNBGU?
faqs.answer: The 2026 policy includes agriculture within its undergraduate scholarship grouping. Awards are limited to tuition; attendance, grades, backlogs and conduct affect continuation. Undergraduate merit scholarships, 2026: The official 2026 policy sets achievement-based categories for its agriculture grouping. Confirm the award and exam-validity conditions; examination and enrolment charges are excluded from scholarship coverage.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for RNBGU?
faqs.answer: The school describes practical and industry exposure as part of career preparation. A dated agriculture-only placement report or salary figure was not established.

faqs.question: How can I contact RNBGU about an application?
faqs.answer: Published phone: 0151 3507600. Published email: admissions@rnbglobal.edu.in. Official admissions: https://www.rnbglobal.edu.in/admission-procedure

faqs.question: Which dated admission notices are recorded for RNBGU?
faqs.answer: University procedure page’s stated admission closing date (past; header still advertises 2026) · 2026-07-30 · 2026-2027. These are the dates of the named events; an earlier deadline does not establish a current opening.

faqs.question: Is T.D. College a university?
faqs.answer: It is an affiliated college. The audited entry identifies Veer Bahadur Singh Purvanchal University as its parent university; the college remains the teaching institution.

faqs.question: Does 1914 mark the start of degree courses?
faqs.answer: No. The history traces the institution to a school established in 1914 and dates degree-college status to July 1947.

faqs.question: Which agriculture master’s subjects are listed by ICAR?
faqs.answer: The audited scope covers agronomy, agricultural economics, agricultural extension education, entomology, genetics and plant breeding, and plant pathology. Each printed master’s intake is 20. These are accreditation entries rather than live vacancy figures.

faqs.question: Why do agriculture degree names and seats differ between pages?
faqs.answer: The ICAR row prints B.S. (Hons). Agriculture with intake 240, while the older department page calls it B.Sc. (Ag) Hons. and shows 220. The current entrance bulletin should settle the name and seats offered for an admission session.

faqs.question: Where can applicants contact the college?
faqs.answer: The official contact page gives Husainabad, Jaunpur 222002, phone +91 7068319555 and principaltdc1914@gmail.com.

faqs.question: Are current agriculture fees published in this draft?
faqs.answer: No. The official fee page displayed an image without a readable year-specific agriculture table. A dated fee schedule is needed to separate tuition, examination and other charges.

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at T.D. College?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; M.Sc. (Ag) Agronomy; M.Sc. (Ag) Agricultural Economics; M.Sc. (Ag) Agricultural Extension Education; M.Sc. (Ag) Entomology; M.Sc. (Ag) Genetics and Plant Breeding; M.Sc. (Ag) Plant Pathology. The [courses and fees table](/university/tilak-dhari-pg-college/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at T.D. College?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). A broad agriculture degree supported by the college’s subject departments.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Ag) Agronomy at T.D. College?
faqs.answer: 2 years (4 semesters). Master’s specialisation in agronomy.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Ag) Agricultural Extension Education at T.D. College?
faqs.answer: 2 years (4 semesters). Master’s specialisation in agricultural extension education.

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Ag) Entomology at T.D. College?

faqs.question: How long is M.Sc. (Ag) Plant Pathology at T.D. College?

sections.heading: Which admission route applies?
paragraphs: Admission to agriculture programmes at Apex University, Jaipur is conducted through Rajasthan JET / CUET (UG) / Apex Common Entrance Test (ACET), alongside direct university merit counselling for eligible 10+2 Agriculture/Science candidates.

Both Rajasthan JET state counselling seats and university-level seats require verification of Class XII subject combinations (PCB, PCM, PCA or Agriculture) and original academic certificates at reporting.

sections.heading: Official channels and public contact details
paragraphs: Use the official channel for the exact programme and quota. Institution contacts below are public source details; ask the office to confirm the intended intake before applying.

sections.heading: Programme-wise eligibility and selection
paragraphs: The following requirements belong to the named programme. A university-wide entrance or eligibility statement should not be transferred to every degree.

rows: 10+2 in Agriculture or Science (PCB / PCM / PCA) with at least 50% aggregate marks (45% for reserved categories).
Rajasthan JET counselling or ACET / CUET merit followed by university verification.
4-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture / Horticulture from a recognized university with minimum 55% aggregate marks.
Rajasthan Pre-PG / ACET postgraduate entrance and academic merit.
Graduation in Agriculture or allied sciences with at least 50% marks.
ACET / CUET-PG / national management score and personal interview.

faqs.question: How does admission to AU Jaipur work?
faqs.answer: Admission to agriculture programmes at Apex University, Jaipur is conducted through Rajasthan JET / CUET (UG) / Apex Common Entrance Test (ACET), alongside direct university merit counselling for eligible 10+2 Agriculture/Science candidates. Both Rajasthan JET state counselling seats and university-level seats require verification of Class XII subject combinations (PCB, PCM, PCA or Agriculture) and original academic certificates at reporting. Check Rajasthan JET or University Application Window: Register through the official Apex University, Jaipur admissions portal (https://www.apexuniversity.co.in/school-of-agricultural-sciences/) or select the institution during Rajasthan JET / Pre-PG choice filling. Submit Academic & Entrance Score Details: Provide Class X and XII mark sheets (or B.Sc. Agriculture transcript for PG), JET/CUET/University entrance scorecard and category certificate. Document Verification & Tuition Fee Confirmation: Verify original documents on campus at Jaipur and obtain the itemised semester/annual fee receipt including hostel and examination heads.

faqs.question: How does admission to AU Jaipur work?
faqs.answer: Admission to agriculture programmes at Apex University, Jaipur is conducted through Rajasthan JET / CUET (UG) / Apex Common Entrance Test (ACET), alongside direct university merit counselling for eligible 10+2 Agriculture/Science candidates. Both Rajasthan JET state counselling seats and university-level seats require verification of Class XII subject combinations (PCB, PCM, PCA or Agriculture) and original academic certificates at reporting. Check Rajasthan JET or University Application Window: Register through the official Apex University, Jaipur admissions portal (https://www.apexuniversity.co.in/school-of-agricultural-sciences/) or select the institution during Rajasthan JET / Pre-PG choice filling. Submit Academic & Entrance Score Details: Provide Class X and XII mark sheets (or B.Sc. Agriculture transcript for PG), JET/CUET/University entrance scorecard and category certificate. Document Verification & Tuition Fee Confirmation: Verify original documents on campus at Jaipur and obtain the itemised semester/annual fee receipt including hostel and examination heads.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for AU Jaipur?
faqs.answer: School of Agricultural Sciences, Apex University, Jaipur: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; M.Sc. Agriculture (Agronomy); MBA Agribusiness Management, recorded term 2022-23 to 2026-27 (UGC / State University Act & Rajasthan JET participating faculty; check ICAR NAEAB cohort notice). This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at AU Jaipur?
faqs.answer: Rural Agricultural Work Experience (RAWE) in adopted villages during the final year. Experiential Learning Programme (ELP) modules in organic inputs, nursery management, Mushroom cultivation and seed production. Field visits to Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), state agricultural research stations and agri-input processing plants in Rajasthan.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at AU Jaipur?
faqs.answer: Agronomy & Instructional Crop Farm: Field demonstration plots at Jaipur for kharif and rabi crop trials, seed bed preparation, weed management and micro-irrigation exercises. Soil Science & Agricultural Chemistry Lab: Equipped for soil pH, electrical conductivity, organic carbon, macronutrient (N-P-K) and micronutrient testing. Horticulture, Polyhouse & Orchard Unit: Protected cultivation polyhouse/shade-net house, fruit orchard nursery and post-harvest handling practical space. Plant Pathology, Entomology & Genetics Labs: Compound and stereo microscopy, insect rearing cages, disease specimen collection and seed purity testing equipment. Student Hostels, Library & Transport: Separate boys and girls residential hostels at Jaipur, agricultural library journals, mess and city bus connectivity.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for AU Jaipur?
faqs.answer: Student Hostels, Library & Transport: Separate boys and girls residential hostels at Jaipur, agricultural library journals, mess and city bus connectivity.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for AU Jaipur?
faqs.answer: Apex University, Jaipur offers merit-based tuition scholarships based on Class XII / qualifying examination marks or JET rank, alongside Rajasthan government post-matric scholarships (SJMS / Samaj Kalyan Vibhag) for eligible SC, ST, OBC, MBC and EBC students. University Entrance & Qualifying Marks Merit Scholarship (2026-27): Tuition fee waiver slabs (10% to 50% in first year) for applicants scoring 75%+ to 90%+ in 10+2 or high rank in Rajasthan JET / CUET; continuation requires maintaining minimum SGPA and 75% attendance. Rajasthan State Post-Matric & Girl Child Agriculture Incentive: Eligible Rajasthan domicile students can apply on the Rajasthan SSO Scholarship Portal; girl students in agriculture may also check state Rajshree / Agriculture Department incentive schemes.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for AU Jaipur?
faqs.answer: The placement and training cell at Apex University, Jaipur coordinates final-year agribusiness agro-industrial attachments, KVK internships and preparation for Rajasthan Agriculture Supervisor, AAO, Pre-PG, ICAR JRF and IBPS AFO competitive examinations. Graduates pursue roles in seed, fertilizer, crop-protection, micro-irrigation, agri-fintech, warehousing and rural banking sectors, as well as M.Sc. Agriculture through Rajasthan Pre-PG and CUET-PG.

faqs.question: How does admission to NIMS Jaipur work?
faqs.answer: Admission to agriculture programmes at NIMS University Rajasthan, Jaipur is conducted through Rajasthan JET / NIMSEE / CUET (UG), alongside direct university merit counselling for eligible 10+2 Agriculture/Science candidates. Both Rajasthan JET state counselling seats and university-level seats require verification of Class XII subject combinations (PCB, PCM, PCA or Agriculture) and original academic certificates at reporting. Check Rajasthan JET or University Application Window: Register through the official NIMS University Rajasthan, Jaipur admissions portal (https://www.nimsuniversity.org/nims-institute-of-agricultural-sciences/) or select the institution during Rajasthan JET / Pre-PG choice filling. Submit Academic & Entrance Score Details: Provide Class X and XII mark sheets (or B.Sc. Agriculture transcript for PG), JET/CUET/University entrance scorecard and category certificate. Document Verification & Tuition Fee Confirmation: Verify original documents on campus at Jaipur and obtain the itemised semester/annual fee receipt including hostel and examination heads.

faqs.question: How does admission to NIMS Jaipur work?
faqs.answer: Admission to agriculture programmes at NIMS University Rajasthan, Jaipur is conducted through Rajasthan JET / NIMSEE / CUET (UG), alongside direct university merit counselling for eligible 10+2 Agriculture/Science candidates. Both Rajasthan JET state counselling seats and university-level seats require verification of Class XII subject combinations (PCB, PCM, PCA or Agriculture) and original academic certificates at reporting. Check Rajasthan JET or University Application Window: Register through the official NIMS University Rajasthan, Jaipur admissions portal (https://www.nimsuniversity.org/nims-institute-of-agricultural-sciences/) or select the institution during Rajasthan JET / Pre-PG choice filling. Submit Academic & Entrance Score Details: Provide Class X and XII mark sheets (or B.Sc. Agriculture transcript for PG), JET/CUET/University entrance scorecard and category certificate. Document Verification & Tuition Fee Confirmation: Verify original documents on campus at Jaipur and obtain the itemised semester/annual fee receipt including hostel and examination heads.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for NIMS Jaipur?
faqs.answer: NIMS Institute of Agricultural Sciences, NIMS University Rajasthan, Jaipur: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; M.Sc. Agriculture (Agronomy); MBA Agribusiness Management, recorded term 2022-23 to 2026-27 (UGC / State University Act & Rajasthan JET participating faculty; check ICAR NAEAB cohort notice). This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at NIMS Jaipur?
faqs.answer: Rural Agricultural Work Experience (RAWE) in adopted villages during the final year. Experiential Learning Programme (ELP) modules in organic inputs, nursery management, Mushroom cultivation and seed production. Field visits to Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), state agricultural research stations and agri-input processing plants in Rajasthan.

faqs.question: Which teaching facilities are documented at NIMS Jaipur?
faqs.answer: Agronomy & Instructional Crop Farm: Field demonstration plots at Jaipur for kharif and rabi crop trials, seed bed preparation, weed management and micro-irrigation exercises. Soil Science & Agricultural Chemistry Lab: Equipped for soil pH, electrical conductivity, organic carbon, macronutrient (N-P-K) and micronutrient testing. Horticulture, Polyhouse & Orchard Unit: Protected cultivation polyhouse/shade-net house, fruit orchard nursery and post-harvest handling practical space. Plant Pathology, Entomology & Genetics Labs: Compound and stereo microscopy, insect rearing cages, disease specimen collection and seed purity testing equipment. Student Hostels, Library & Transport: Separate boys and girls residential hostels at Jaipur, agricultural library journals, mess and city bus connectivity.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for NIMS Jaipur?
faqs.answer: Student Hostels, Library & Transport: Separate boys and girls residential hostels at Jaipur, agricultural library journals, mess and city bus connectivity.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for NIMS Jaipur?
faqs.answer: NIMS University Rajasthan, Jaipur offers merit-based tuition scholarships based on Class XII / qualifying examination marks or JET rank, alongside Rajasthan government post-matric scholarships (SJMS / Samaj Kalyan Vibhag) for eligible SC, ST, OBC, MBC and EBC students. University Entrance & Qualifying Marks Merit Scholarship (2026-27): Tuition fee waiver slabs (10% to 50% in first year) for applicants scoring 75%+ to 90%+ in 10+2 or high rank in Rajasthan JET / CUET; continuation requires maintaining minimum SGPA and 75% attendance. Rajasthan State Post-Matric & Girl Child Agriculture Incentive: Eligible Rajasthan domicile students can apply on the Rajasthan SSO Scholarship Portal; girl students in agriculture may also check state Rajshree / Agriculture Department incentive schemes.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for NIMS Jaipur?
faqs.answer: The placement and training cell at NIMS University Rajasthan, Jaipur coordinates final-year agribusiness agro-industrial attachments, KVK internships and preparation for Rajasthan Agriculture Supervisor, AAO, Pre-PG, ICAR JRF and IBPS AFO competitive examinations. Graduates pursue roles in seed, fertilizer, crop-protection, micro-irrigation, agri-fintech, warehousing and rural banking sectors, as well as M.Sc. Agriculture through Rajasthan Pre-PG and CUET-PG.
